preconditions.description: n is the number of distinct passwords (1 ≤ n ≤ 100), and k is the number of failed tries before a 5-second delay (1 ≤ k ≤ 100).

preconditions.expression: all(len(password) <= 100 for password in passwords) and all(password.isalnum() for password in passwords)
preconditions.description: Each password is a non-empty string of Latin letters and digits with length ≤ 100.
The correct password is guaranteed to be one of the n passwords.

postconditions.description: The output consists of two integers: the minimum possible time (best_case) and the maximum possible time (worst_case) for Vanya to enter the correct password.

postconditions.expression: min_time == sum(1 for _ in range(1 + position_of_correct_in_best_order)) + 5 * (number_of_full_k_blocks_in_best_order)
postconditions.description: The best-case time is the sum of 1 second per attempt until the correct password is entered, plus 5 seconds for every full block of k failed attempts before the correct one. The correct password is entered as early as possible in the sorted order.

postconditions.expression: max_time == sum(1 for _ in range(1 + position_of_correct_in_worst_order)) + 5 * (number_of_full_k_blocks_in_worst_order)
postconditions.description: The worst-case time is the sum of 1 second per attempt until the correct password is entered, plus 5 seconds for every full block of k failed attempts before the correct one. The correct password is entered as late as possible in the sorted order.

postconditions.expression: position_of_correct_in_best_order == min(i for i, password in enumerate(sorted_passwords) if password == correct_password)
postconditions.description: The best-case position is the earliest index of the correct password in the sorted list of passwords by non-decreasing length.

postconditions.expression: position_of_correct_in_worst_order == max(i for i, password in enumerate(sorted_passwords) if password == correct_password)
postconditions.description: The worst-case position is the latest index of the correct password in the sorted list of passwords by non-decreasing length.
The number of full k-blocks in the best case is the integer division of (position - 1) by k.
